title: Gameplay Banter Catalog
description: English alternatives for private notifications to the player performing an action and, when useful, the player affected by it. Stable English IDs support integration and future localization.
scope: Complete copy catalog with suggested activation rules. It does not claim which mechanics are already implemented in the project. Connect this JSON to the game's event system; it is not an Unreal DataTable ready to import without adaptation.
editorial_guidelines: Friendly FPS banter: joke about the play, the mistake, or the situation, not the person's worth.
Use more sarcasm for friendly fire and self-inflicted mishaps; keep repeated-death messages lighter and encouraging.
Do not imply rewards for friendly fire or invent penalties. These are messages, not changes to scoring or match rules.
No discriminatory insults, personal-attribute references, cheating accusations, or invented explanations involving lag or bugs.

Keep HUD lines short and easy to understand at a glance. Prefer common English words and concrete jokes about the action; avoid obscure idioms and abstract business metaphors. The separate title clearly identifies the event.
Keep titles and messages private to their recipient, including normal personal summary screens. Do not automatically post them in public chat.

format_guide.event_lookup: Look up events by id. Do not use an event's array position as its identifier.
format_guide.roles: actor is the event's stated protagonist: the killer, the player making a mistake, or, for death/respawn/results, the player experiencing that situation. target is the explicitly defined second recipient, never inferred from player order.
format_guide.message_arrays: messages.actor and messages.target are independent lists of alternatives. Matching indices do NOT form pairs.
format_guide.empty_arrays: An empty array means no notification for that recipient. Do not copy text from the other array or automatically activate kill as a fallback.
format_guide.variant_ids: Message IDs are stable: event_id.audience.NN. After a version has shipped, do not reuse a deleted message's ID for different copy.
format_guide.display: title is the event label; the selected variant is the short message. Priority, duration, and cooldown are adjustable suggestions.
format_guide.not_implemented: trigger describes a condition to connect to actual game events. No expression in this JSON is executable code.

activation.rule: An event is eligible only if enabled_by_default is true or it has been explicitly enabled, ALL capabilities in requires are available in the current mode, and its trigger is satisfied.
activation.default_profile: A restrained profile for deathmatch and team deathmatch. Even enabled events require real telemetry: never infer a noscope, wallbang, or reflected hit from an impression.
activation.quiet_defaults_reason: These messages are included, but showing them on every kill, death, or respawn can overwhelm the HUD. Enable them for a more talkative profile.

tuning.literal_number_warning: The double/triple/quad/penta, killstreak, domination, and death_streak messages name exact quantities. If you change those thresholds, update the labels, triggers, and related messages too. Other tuning values are proposed parameters, not verified project settings.

procedure: Filter for alternatives that can be rendered with the available context.
Shuffle variant IDs with a random number generator and keep a separate bag for each player, event, and audience.
Draw without replacement only when a notification is actually displayed.
When the bag is empty, reshuffle. With at least two alternatives, ensure the next bag's first message differs from the last message shown.
If a variant is temporarily unusable because a placeholder is missing, keep it available for a future valid context.
Do not use the same index for actor and target. Their arrays may have different lengths and must be sampled independently.
selection_policy.missing_context: If a placeholder is unavailable, choose a variant from the same array that does not need it. If none can be used, omit the joke and keep only the informative label. Never display unresolved braces.

length.overflow: Shorten names with an ellipsis first. Allow at most two lines in the layout. Check width using the actual font, not just the character count.

selection_policy.rendering: Insert placeholders as plain text without interpreting markup in player names. For {team}, use the actual team name, such as Alpha or Omega.

presentation_policy.scope: At most one main toast for the same occurrence and recipient. Related kill, death, and assist contexts must share a correlation.
presentation_policy.priority_rule: Among eligible candidates for the recipient, the higher display.priority wins. Break ties by event id in lexicographic order for a stable result.
presentation_policy.cooldown_rule: An event suppressed by cooldown must not be replaced by a more generic variant of the same occurrence. The attacker's cooldown must not silence a notification due to another victim.
presentation_policy.presentation_only: Suppressing copy does not undo statistics, milestones, revenge consumption, or domination-state changes.
presentation_policy.simultaneous_kills: Aggregate victims of the same projectile or explosion first. Show the selected recognition with the final count, without a burst of double/triple/quad notifications for one blast.
presentation_policy.successive_multikills: For kills separated in time, update the same chain's toast to the level reached rather than stacking copies. A higher-priority event may replace it.
presentation_policy.friendly_fire: Do not generate headshot, multikill, killstreak, revenge, or other enemy-kill awards for the same allied death. Keep a useful friendly-fire label even when the joke is on cooldown.
presentation_policy.mixed_explosions: If one action hits allies and enemies, show the attacker the friendly-fire warning first. Valid enemy kills retain their credit. Each victim evaluates only their own relationship with the attacker.
presentation_policy.target_silence: An event with an empty messages.target array does not authorize a substitute target message. Only other distinct, genuinely applicable events may notify that player, such as death_while_reloading.
presentation_policy.status_banners: Phase and timer warnings retain essential information. Omit the joke if it would occupy space needed for a more important notification. Do not build long queues of stale jokes.
presentation_policy.results: The final result takes precedence over leftover toasts. MVP uses a separate award_panel so it can appear alongside the result on the final screen without overlap.

headshot_example.reason: With the proposed priorities, 88 takes precedence over 76 and 60.
headshot_example.target: Only the revenge target variants, if that event is valid and not on cooldown.

event_accounting: Use server-confirmed events and stable identifiers. Deduplicate replicated kills before updating counters or notifications. Preserve the victim's pre-death streak snapshot before resetting it.
Multikill means rapid eliminations: with the proposed settings, at most 4 seconds between consecutive kills. Killstreak means kills within one life, with no time limit. Keep the counters separate.

Every death ends the life and resets the rapid chain and current streak. Match start and new rounds reset life counters. Suicides and teamkills do not add enemy eliminations; a teamkill does not become an award.

Projectiles retain the identity of the life that created them. A posthumous kill belongs to the old life even after a respawn. It may count toward match totals, but must not reopen closed chains or streaks, add to the new life's counters, or consume the new life's revenge or comeback opportunity.

Track deaths without kills across the player's sequence: killing an enemy during the active life resets the counter; a posthumous kill does not. Match start and team changes reset the sequence. The notifications at 3 and 5 deaths are optional and private.

Revenge: remember the last valid enemy killer, keep the opportunity after unrelated kills, and consume it on the first valid kill against that enemy. Every new death replaces the reference; a death without a valid enemy killer clears it.

Domination: A killing B increments A→B and resets B→A. After four unanswered kills, A dominates B; announce only the transition. A reverse kill breaks domination. Interactions with third parties do not reset the pair. A new match, team change, or permanent departure invalidates the relevant states.

Milestones and recognition consumption still occur when another notification wins priority. Do not postpone an already-consumed revenge event until a later kill. Advance the shuffle bag only for messages actually displayed.
Multi-victim aggregates use kill_count or unnamed wording. Never arbitrarily select one victim as target. Single-player references always use the specific event's context.
Scoring, penalties, assists, and MVP rules remain defined by gameplay. This catalog adds copy and suggested conditions, not rewards, damage, kicks, or sanctions.

actor.meaning: Display name of the protagonist specified in roles.actor.

target.meaning: Name of the individual target for this action. For teammate_saved, this is the rescued ally.

kill_count.meaning: Chain total for multikill; enemies killed by the same grenade for grenade_multikill; victims of the same projectile for collateral. Never allies.

streak_count.meaning: For shutdown, the victim's streak immediately before death. Do not use the attacker's streak.

distance_m.meaning: Distance of the lethal hit, rounded to whole meters for display.

health.meaning: The attacker's positive remaining HP when the kill is confirmed. Round fractional HP up so a living player is not shown as having 0 HP.

team.meaning: Team name of the player receiving the result.

seconds.meaning: Seconds remaining when the warning threshold is crossed.
